q1_layer_recommendation: c (hybrid: mapper emits a synthetic subagent_lifecycle virtual tool-call envelope; the three real spawn/wait/close ToolViews are suppressed in the main flow when the synthetic lifecycle envelope owns the receiverThreadId). Justification: the mapper already builds the only piece of cross-event identity that matters — sessionSubagent — at sessionProtocolMapper.ts:651-660. It is the ONLY layer that sees collab_agent_call_begin/end events in canonical order with the receiverThreadId and the call_id intact. Doing the merge there avoids inventing brittle adjacency heuristics in the renderer (which has no list-level sibling view; ChatList feeds one message at a time at ChatList.tsx:48). Pure CLI-rewrite (option a) is too aggressive — it deletes information the spawn_agent inner TaskStatusRow already needs (sessionSubagent driving CodexSubagentView at CodexSubagentView.tsx:38-42), and it breaks old encrypted message blobs that were emitted as three envelopes pre-cycle-2. Pure renderer (option b) needs a stateful pre-pass over the message list before ChatList renderItem fires, which doesn't exist today (ChatList.tsx wires sessions.messages directly into FlashList data). The hybrid keeps the existing 3-envelope path intact (so old sessions render as before via fallback), but emits an additional 4th 'lifecycle' tool-call message keyed by sessionSubagent. The renderer suppresses the three control envelopes when they belong to a sessionSubagent that has a lifecycle envelope present, and renders the lifecycle card instead. Blast radius is bounded: one new view, one new envelope name, one suppression check; the existing CodexSubagentView, knownTools entries, and CODEX_SUBAGENT_CONTROL_TOOLS gate stay as fallbacks for old messages.

a_cli_mapper_collapse.blast_radius: high — sessionProtocolMapper.ts collab_agent_call_begin (sessionProtocolMapper.ts:646) becomes a buffering state machine: must hold spawn until matching close arrives, must ignore wait_agent end as terminal, must mutate currentTurnId pre-existing envelopes; turn-end and turn_aborted (sessionProtocolMapper.ts:437-462) must flush pending lifecycle so subagent lifecycle never leaks across turns
a_cli_mapper_collapse.old_message_compat: BREAKING — encrypted SessionMessage blobs from cycles 1/2/3 already on the server contain three separate tool-call envelopes; this option does not change them, so OLD sessions still render as 3 cards. Mismatch between old and new sessions becomes a permanent UI difference
a_cli_mapper_collapse.testability: moderate — sessionProtocolMapper.ts has clean unit-test surface (tests/codex/sessionProtocolMapper.test.ts pattern) but state-machine paths multiply: spawn-no-wait, spawn-wait-close, spawn-close (no wait), spawn-then-turn-end (close never arrives)
a_cli_mapper_collapse.failure_mode_missing_intermediate: spawn arrives but wait/close never arrive within the turn — mapper holds an open lifecycle that never completes; spinner-running symptom returns
a_cli_mapper_collapse.verdict: rejected — too much risk to a hot mapper code path that just stabilized in cycle 2; breaks encryption-blob retroactivity

b_app_renderer_pre_pass.blast_radius: moderate — needs a new pre-pass over messages array to compute lifecycleGroupId before ChatList feeds FlashList data; either wraps ChatList.tsx:48 with a memoized grouping selector, or exposes a derived field on Message in the sync reducer
b_app_renderer_pre_pass.old_message_compat: WORKS for both old and new sessions because pre-pass works on stored ToolCall.input.sessionSubagent which is already present in cycle-2 mapper output (sessionProtocolMapper.ts:684 args spreads sessionSubagent)
b_app_renderer_pre_pass.testability: good — pure function on Message[] => Message[] grouping is unit-testable; can drive renderer with synthetic 3-card sequences
b_app_renderer_pre_pass.failure_mode_missing_intermediate: graceful — if wait or close is missing, the lifecycle card freezes at the last known state; pre-pass walks messages in order, no buffer-across-turn problem because turn boundaries are visible in Message[]
b_app_renderer_pre_pass.verdict: second choice — cleaner than a but introduces a new rendering concept (group selector) and adds latency to every ChatList render (O(n) scan); the hybrid achieves the same effect with less work

c_hybrid_synthetic_lifecycle_envelope.blast_radius: low — one new envelope name (e.g., functions.subagent_lifecycle), one new view (CodexSubagentLifecycleView), one new suppression check in CodexSubagentView/codexToolRendering.ts; the existing 3 cards keep their entries in toolViewRegistry as fallback
c_hybrid_synthetic_lifecycle_envelope.old_message_compat: PERFECT — old sessions never received the synthetic envelope, so they render as 3 cards (status: cycle-2 stable). New sessions render with the lifecycle card and the 3 underlying cards are suppressed
c_hybrid_synthetic_lifecycle_envelope.testability: good — fixture page (codex-render-fixtures-data.ts:181-204) already has spawnAgentTool/waitAgentTool/closeAgentTool; one new fixture row 'subagent-lifecycle-merged' pairs a synthetic lifecycle ToolCall with sessionSubagent='codex-fixture-subagent' and asserts the three control tools collapse
c_hybrid_synthetic_lifecycle_envelope.failure_mode_missing_intermediate: graceful — if spawn arrives without wait/close, lifecycle envelope is emitted with status='running' or 'started' (mapper holds it until turn-end emits terminal). If turn-end fires before close, lifecycle envelope is upgraded to 'cancelled' on turn-end. The 3 underlying cards are still emitted in their original positions for retroactive transparency
c_hybrid_synthetic_lifecycle_envelope.verdict: RECOMMENDED — minimum blast radius, perfect retroactive compat, leverages existing mapper state (providerSubagentToSessionSubagent map), preserves cycle-2 stability for fallback

running.note: no separate envelope is emitted — mapper mutates the existing lifecycle envelope's args.lifecycle_state via a synthetic tool-call-update intermediate (or simpler: the renderer derives state from presence of wait/close in the same group)

ready.trigger_envelope: tool-call-end for wait_agent for the same sessionSubagent

q2_state_machine.transition_diagram: started -> running (on wait_begin) -> ready (on wait_end) -> completed (on close_end) | started -> errored (on any end with !=completed) | started/running -> errored (on turn-end before close_end)

a_spawn_then_close_no_wait.behavior: mapper detects close_end for sessionSubagent without prior wait_begin -> emits lifecycle tool-call-end directly with status=completed (or whatever close.status is), duration = close_end - spawn_start; UI skips 'running'/'ready' states and goes started -> completed

b_parallel_subagents_interleaved.behavior: providerSubagentToSessionSubagent map keys by callSubagentKey(callId), so each spawn creates a distinct sessionSubagent. The mapper holds lifecycle state in a Map<sessionSubagent, LifecycleState> instead of a single slot. Two parallel subagents A and B produce two synthetic lifecycle envelopes with disjoint sessionSubagent keys; the renderer suppresses spawn/wait/close cards independently per sessionSubagent. Order within a single subagent's lifecycle is preserved by Codex's serial emission of begin/end pairs even when interleaved across subagents
b_parallel_subagents_interleaved.implementation_note: the mapper state CodexTurnState (sessionProtocolMapper.ts:8-13) MUST be extended with subagentLifecycles?: Map<string, { spawnCallId, waitCallId, closeCallId, lifecycleEnvelopeCall, state }>

c_old_messages_no_lifecycle_envelope.behavior: old encrypted SessionMessage blobs do not contain functions.subagent_lifecycle envelopes — they only have spawn/wait/close. Renderer's suppression check is conditional: 'if a lifecycle envelope exists for this sessionSubagent, suppress the 3 control envelopes; otherwise render them as the cycle-2 fallback'. The check executes per ChatList renderItem by reading a memoized derived map sessionSubagent -> hasLifecycleEnvelope built once per messages[] update
c_old_messages_no_lifecycle_envelope.implementation_note: this preserves the cycle-2 invariant 'each card correct, spinner stops, position stable' for old sessions verbatim

d_close_agent_dropped_or_timeout.behavior: two failure modes: (1) close_agent never arrives but turn ends — task_complete or turn_aborted (sessionProtocolMapper.ts:437) flushes lifecycles by upgrading any non-terminal lifecycle to 'errored' with status='cancelled' or whatever pickTurnEndStatus returns. (2) close_agent ends with error status — mapper emits lifecycle tool-call-end with state='errored' and output containing the error. UI shows 'Failed' with timestamp frozen and ToolError body
